result.title: Decision language models as affordable and rapid alternatives to LLM judges of clinical generative AI
result.summary: Automated judges of clinical artificial intelligence (AI) outputs are necessary, but large language model (LLM) judges are costly and slow at scale. We compared Jev, a decision language model that returns structured judgments, with frontier and open-weight LLM judges in four use cases. On 118 pediatric answers, Jev's agreement with physicians' ordinal quality ratings (Gwet's AC2 0.50; expected score 0.53) matched or exceeded that of seven of 12 LLM judges, including frontier models, Claude Opus 5.5 (0.49) and GPT-6 (0.38). On physician-graded binary HealthBench criteria, Jev matched or exceeded four of six LLM judges. On MedHELM's open-ended tasks, Jev's agreement with a three-LLM jury approached or exceeded the jurors' internal agreement. On HealthBench Professional, Jev matched the benchmark's reference judge, GPT-5.4, on 91% of criteria (other judges, 91-93%). Frontier judges cost 73-294 times more than Jev and took 7-57 times longer. Jev may enable efficient clinical AI evaluation at scale.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在四个临床 AI 输出评判场景中，比较返回结构化判定结果的决策语言模型 Jev 与前沿及开源 LLM 评判者，发现其与医师评分的一致性接近或超过多数 LLM 评判者，而成本低 73–294 倍、耗时短 7–57 倍。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是临床文本评判而非视觉或多模态推理，但「低成本、结构化输出的判定模型」可能可供核查能否充当 latent 推理轨迹的廉价验证器或停止判据，其成本与延迟对照也提示 LVR 评价中的实际开销问题。
